claims.content: Customer

At the main-flow step where the Customer is about to confirm payment, if the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button/radio button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a warning that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) and that unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires.

If a PayPal/Amazon Payments order is not paid within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction's closing date/time, the order is cancelled and the item is placed into 'Hold' status; the Customer cannot pay to unlock the cancelled order. Exit: use case terminates in cancellation; no payment is completed.

missing_aspects: exact main-flow step numbers for anchoring exception branches
payment-processing error handling (e.g., declined payment, invalid payment details, gateway failure)
Evidence for the specific exit condition: 'use case terminates without completing payment; the Customer may return to complete payment within the 7-day window.'

claims.content: Diverges from Step 1: For a 2nd-Chance offer item, the Customer accepts the offer by clicking the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button in the automated email, which triggers an automated process to generate the order and ship the item without further action.

Diverges from Step 1: For a 2nd-Chance offer item, the Customer clicks the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button in the automated email; the system generates the order, loads the Sign-In page, and after signing in takes the Customer to the Returning Winners Payments Page to pay for the order.

Diverges from Step 1: The Customer can also reach the Returning Winners Payments page by clicking the Winnings Alert link, which is available from the My Account page, My Watch List, My Current Bids, My Bid History, and the Safe Shopping Guarantee page.

Diverges from Step 1: If the Customer's default payment method is PayPal, the system sends an email notification upon winning and the Customer must manually log into their JTV account to process payment within 7 days.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of the standard page display, returning users with a default Method of Payment of PayPal or Amazon Payments are routed to a specific page that offers them a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for their winnings.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may select PayPal as the payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section.

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may pay by entering a credit card in the 'My New Payment Method' section, including new billing address details (Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country).

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering the Country (defaulted to United States), and choosing 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card' as the payment method.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may log in using the email and password fields on the right side of the page to complete payment rather than creating a new account or using Amazon Payments.
Customer completes payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer completes payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer selects the won items to pay for, chooses a shipping method, chooses a payment type, and completes the transaction.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer is at the checkout/payment flow for won auction items with items available to select for payment.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer has selected the desired items, shipping method, and payment type, and the transaction is completed.
in_scope_actions: Choose which won auction items to pay for
excluded_adjacent_actions: Administrative order management or cancellation processing
variant_dimensions: Which won items the Customer selects for payment

claims.content: For items where the transaction has been successfully completed, the 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid'.

After completing an Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The Customer has at least one won auction item for which payment has not yet been completed, so there are items available to select for payment.
The Customer's account must not be locked or in Review Status; an eligible account status (not locked, not under review) is required before checkout can begin.

Before any 2nd-Chance offer checkout path can be triggered, a 2nd-Chance offer must exist for the Customer (e.g., as the second-place finisher after the original order was cancelled); and for the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' trigger path, the Customer must already have a credit card stored on their account.
The Customer chooses which items to pay for from the list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.
The Customer selects a checkout option for the chosen payment method by clicking the corresponding button.

The Customer completes the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, or, for a 2nd-Chance offer, clicks the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button in the automated email, which triggers an automated process to generate an order and ship the item, or clicks the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button in the automated email, which generates the order and loads the Sign-In page for payment. For Amazon/PayPal completions, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page; for On File credit card completions, an order is automatically generated and shipped. After any successful completion, the Payment Status column displays 'Paid' for the items where the transaction has been successfully completed.

The Customer starts the checkout/payment flow by clicking a payment-initiation link/button: the 'Pay Now' link in the winner notification email, the 'Winnings Alert' link, the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button (for a 2nd-Chance offer item), or the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button (for a 2nd-Chance offer item).

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger includes 2nd-Chance-offer email buttons ('I accept, pay with my On File credit card' and 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments') as entry points, but Main Flow step 1 assumes the Customer starts by selecting items from the won-items list and then choosing shipping. For the On File 2nd-Chance path, the trigger itself executes payment/order generation, so steps 1–5 cannot apply; for the PayPal/Amazon 2nd-Chance path, the email button generates the order and goes to Sign-In, again not through the won-items/shipping selection. Thus the linear main flow does not continue from those 2nd-Chance triggers.

inconsistency_hints: Preconditions refers to account status/Review Status as a condition but does not assert the required state. The checkout trigger can be initiated only if the Customer's account is not locked and not in review; that independent state is not actually covered.

Main Flow ends at selecting a checkout option and never includes completion of the payment transaction. Postcondition 1 (Payment Status displays Paid) and postcondition 2 (Thank You page after completing Amazon/PayPal checkout) both depend on a completed payment, so the Main Flow as written does not reasonably lead to the postconditions.

Goal states 'Customer completes payment for won auction items,' but the main_flow's 5 steps only cover selecting items, choosing a shipping method, and selecting a checkout option. There is no main_flow step in which the payment transaction is completed/confirmed; main_flow ends at step 5 with the Customer selecting a checkout option. Thus the goal's completion claim is not aligned with the behavior actually described in main_flow.

Trigger includes payment-initiation buttons for a 2nd-Chance offer item, but Main Flow step 1 only covers selecting won auction items from a list via Pay Now checkboxes. For the 2nd-Chance trigger variants, the Main Flow restarts as a different won-item selection scenario instead of continuing from the offered item.

Preconditions only mention unpaid won auction items and an eligible account status. The Trigger also includes 2nd-Chance offer items, which are not necessarily won items, and an On File credit card button, which requires the Customer to already have a stored card on the account. Those states are not established before the Trigger.

The Trigger allows checkout to start from 2nd-Chance offer items and from the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button, but the Main Flow only describes selecting won items from a list and completing an Amazon/PayPal checkout. Step 1 and Step 6 therefore do not continue the 2nd-Chance/On File trigger path.
